title.narrative: Output 4.2. Strengthened capacity of enterprises to adopt new business models, technology and techniques to enhance productivity and sustainability

description.narrative: 8000 Cambodian youth, women, entrepreneurs, small business owners, TVET students, vulnerable groups, and marginalized groups have received trainings on productivity, entrepreneurship, innovation and enterprise sustainability, through the ILO's Activity-Based Learning (ABL) programmes and Know About Business (KAB). These programmes are adopted and implemented by the Ministry of Education, Youth and Sports (MoEYS), the Ministry of Tourism (MoT), the Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training (MLVT), the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), University of South-East Asia (USEA), CamEd Business school, GIZ, and 19 different CSOs in Cambodia throughout 2020-2021. UNV, UNDP, UNESCO, UNICEF, UNIDO in Cambodia are in collaborative relationship with the ILO to promote entrepreneurship and skills development under the Decent Employment for Youth initiative. A follow-up survey in December 2020 showed that the trainings improved their entrepreneurial mind-set (75%), Problem solving skill (73%), Communication skill (80%), and Teamwork skill (77%). The training activities contributed to the national development strategies of Cambodia, especially the National Education Strategic Plan (2019-2023). With support of the Government of Japan, Swiss Development Cooperation Agency(SDC) and the Government of Sweden, the ILO has provided the Government and local partners with its capacity development tools to promote productivity, innovation, entrepreneurship and enterprise sustainability, such as Community-Based Enterprise Development(C-BED), Ready-for-Business(R4B), Our.COOP, Factory Improvement Toolkit(FIT), Know About Business(KAB), Start and Improve Your Business (SIYB), Sustaining Competitive and Responsible Enterprises (SCORE).
